hook: A news website asks readers to vote on a new law, and 85% of 50,000 votes say no. That sounds decisive. But who votes in an online poll? Mostly people with strong feelings, often angry ones. A biased method gives the wrong answer however many people take part, and the only cure is a better method.

options: The list the sample is drawn from
prereq.why: The frame is the list of individuals the sample is chosen from.

prereq.q: Which uses chance to choose individuals?
prereq.why: Only the simple random sample uses a chance process.

figure.caption: A sample can go wrong at three points: the frame can leave people out (undercoverage), chosen people can fail to respond (nonresponse), and answers can be untrue (response bias).

chain.cause: A method that lets people choose themselves, or picks whoever is easy to reach
chain.effect: over-represents some kinds of people: voluntary response or convenience sampling

chain.cause: A frame that misses part of the population
chain.effect: those people have no chance of being chosen: undercoverage

chain.cause: Chosen people who do not respond, or who answer untruthfully because of wording or pressure
chain.effect: nonresponse and response bias, even in a random sample

chain.cause: Each of these pushes results the same way every time
chain.effect: the method is biased, and a larger sample does not fix it

ideas: A sampling method is biased if it systematically overestimates or underestimates the value it is trying to estimate.
Voluntary response samples (people choose to answer) and convenience samples (easy to reach) are not random and are usually biased.

Undercoverage: part of the population is missing from the frame. Nonresponse: chosen individuals do not respond. Response bias: answers are not true, from leading wording, sensitive questions or pressure.
Name the bias, explain how the sample differs from the population, and give the likely direction. A larger sample never removes bias.

misconception.wrong: The online poll got 50,000 votes, so its result must be close to the truth.
misconception.right: A voluntary response sample is biased toward strong opinions. More votes give a more precise answer to the wrong question; only a random sample from the population fixes the method.

summary: Bias is a systematic error in a sampling method. Voluntary response and convenience samples are biased because they are not random; undercoverage, nonresponse and response bias can affect even random samples. To explain a bias, name it, say how the sample differs from the population and in which direction, and remember that a bigger sample does not cure it.
